video_title: Cavs Training Camp | Craig Porter Jr. Media Availability | 10.03.2026

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on his leadership role for the second unit
quotes.excerpt: I want to set the tone and let everybody know I can be the leader of a second unit
quotes.quote: I want to set the tone and let everybody know I can be the leader of a second unit and just impact winning basketball, whether it be scoring or doing a lot of the little things I do. And again, making that impact and just making my presence felt and just being more of a vocal leader.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. is embracing a larger role for the Cavs second unit this season. He says he wants to set the tone and impact winning basketball by being a more vocal leader.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on learning defensive accountability from Dennis Schroder
quotes.excerpt: he made his presence felt defensively like he's picking guys up, he's holding guys accountable
quotes.quote: I learned from Dennis Schroder last year. He was more of a quiet guy, but he made his presence felt defensively like he's picking guys up, he's holding guys accountable. I know I'm going into my fourth year, but there's times where Don might do something and I might say something like, 'Hey Don, we got to pick this up a little bit.' So just being able to make everybody around me coachable and actually having a voice and making sure everybody hears me.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. says he is taking lessons from Dennis Schroder on defensive accountability. He plans to be more vocal on the floor and hold his teammates to a higher standard this year.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on the opportunity following roster changes
quotes.excerpt: something has to happen for somebody else to get an opportunity
quotes.quote: In this job you hate to see guys go, but it's kind of how it is. Something has to happen for somebody else to get an opportunity. It's another step in my journey. It's literally that process all over again, just giving me an opportunity to showcase the things I can do and the things I've worked on for the last two or three years.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. views the Cavs roster changes as another step in his journey. He says it is an opportunity to showcase the things he has worked on for the last few years.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on developing as a vocal leader
quotes.excerpt: what are you going to do when you're put in a position to lead or be that head guy
quotes.quote: Everybody realizes you can do all the other little things and all the intangible things, but what are you going to do when you're put in a position to lead or be that head guy in the group? Can you lead these guys? Can you call a play when something else is happening? Can you run this group? I've done a great job of understanding how to do these things and just learning from Don and James and just figuring those things out.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. is focused on proving he can lead a group. He says he has been learning from Donovan Mitchell and James Harden to better understand how to run a team and call plays.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on the coaching staff's focus on intentionality
quotes.excerpt: they just making everything that we do intentional
quotes.quote: They just making everything that we do intentional. So if we're working on shooting, shoot it. Don't waste a rep, don't play around with it because at the end of the day, yes, this is a job but this is your career. You want to take full control of it and you want to be able to understand like, okay, if I'm doing this move, it's going to be a shot I'm going to actually take in the game.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. says the Cavs coaching staff is emphasizing intentionality in training camp. He notes that every rep is treated as if it were a real game shot.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on the potential benefits of NBA Europe
quotes.excerpt: it'll give them the same type of understanding of how the NBA is played
quotes.quote: I feel like it'll be beneficial for guys. It'll give them the same type of understanding of how the NBA is played, but they'll be able to be over here and just experience a lot of the different culture and just how the game's played in a different way. Sometimes in your career you'll have to fill a role or you'll have to be that main guy, and sometimes guys could go overseas and be the Donovan Mitchell and they can figure out how they can score, how they can be a better player, or they can also come over here and be a Sam Merrill, they can be a catch-and-shoot guy who can affect the game in so many different ways.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. believes NBA Europe could be beneficial for player development. He says it offers players a chance to experience different roles and learn how the game is played in a different way.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on finding his path through defensive effort
quotes.excerpt: the only way you're going to get on the court is defense
quotes.quote: When I came out of college and I was doing a lot of my pre-draft workouts, coaches told me straight up, everybody in the NBA is getting looked at because they can score or their offense. So the only way you're going to get on the court is defense. I understood that a lot of the things that would get me on the court are the little things: hustling, playing defense, and rebounding too. That's one of the things I'm good at at my size, and just understanding that plays a big role into it and it'll allow you to pick your spots.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. knows his path to the court is built on defense. He says he learned early on that hustling and rebounding are the little things that allow him to pick his spots in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on the importance of backup point guard depth
quotes.excerpt: it gives those guys a lot of pressure relief
quotes.quote: I feel like being that backup ball-handler and backup point guard is big because it gives those guys a lot of pressure relief. We all know when the playoffs come, James is going to get double-teamed, Don is going to get double-teamed. That's going to be every team's main focus. So just being able to give us a different look and just give them guys some pressure relief because sometimes it can be hard on them.
quotes.social_post: Craig Porter Jr. emphasizes the importance of backup point guard depth. He says his goal is to provide pressure relief for Donovan Mitchell and James Harden when they face double teams in the playoffs.
